Report Title Slide.report_title: General Corporate Operations - Cash Management and Expense Controls

Objective, Background and Scope.purpose_objective: Assess design effectiveness and operating efficiency of cash management and employee expense controls to determine adequacy of procedures, segregation of duties and compliance with corporate policy.
Objective, Background and Scope.background: The corporate treasury and accounts payable functions manage daily cash positioning, disbursements and employee expense reimbursements. Effective controls are required to mitigate fraud, misstatement and regulatory non-compliance. Prior internal audits noted control weaknesses in these areas.
Objective, Background and Scope.scope: Fieldwork covered cash disbursements, bank reconciliations, petty cash, and employee expense reimbursements for the period 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31. Sample testing: 30 bank reconciliations (monthly), 40 cash disbursement transactions, and 30 employee expense claims across all business units.

Overall Internal Audit Rating.overall_conclusion_description: Control environment exhibits control design but inconsistent operating effectiveness leading to increased residual risk for unauthorized disbursements and policy non-compliance. Management has implemented some mitigations but additional remediation is required to reduce exposure to financial loss and regulatory risk.

Observation Slides.observation_title: Inadequate segregation of duties in cash disbursement workflow
Observation Slides.details: In a sample of 40 cash disbursement transactions, 10 (25%) were processed where the same individual initiated the payment request, approved the release in the ERP and executed the bank transfer. System roles permit combined 'Initiate/Approve/Execute' rights in 3 user accounts. Documentation shows only ad-hoc compensating reviews.
Observation Slides.risk_impact: Concentration of duties increases risk of unauthorized or fraudulent payments and misstatement of cash balances. Potential financial loss observed: one unsupported payment of $7,500 was identified during testing.
Observation Slides.recommendations: Restrict system roles to enforce segregation: separate Initiator, Approver and Payment Execution roles. Implement four-eyes approval for disbursements above threshold $5,000. Configure automated approval workflows and enable audit logging with periodic review.
Observation Slides.management_response_action_plan: Treasury will reconfigure ERP role matrices and implement segregation of duties controls. Target date: 2026-04-30. Remediation owner: Head of Treasury, Jane Alvarez. Implementation includes role change, testing and retraining. Quarterly review of audit logs to be assigned to Internal Controls Analyst starting 2026-05-15.

Observation Slides.observation_title: Non-compliance with expense policy and insufficient supporting documentation
Observation Slides.details: In a sample of 30 employee expense claims, 8 claims (27%) lacked required original receipts or had receipts exceeding policy per diem limits. Total value of non-compliant claims: $6,420. Approval stamps were missing on 5 of these claims and 3 claims were approved after payment date.
Observation Slides.risk_impact: Increases likelihood of payroll/expenditure inaccuracies, potential tax/reporting issues and reputational risk. Weak documentation undermines ability to recover or justify VAT and other tax recoveries worth approximately $1,120 in the sample.
Observation Slides.recommendations: Enforce policy through system validation requiring receipt upload prior to approval. Introduce flagging for late approvals and automated query workflow for incomplete claims. Provide refresher training and update expense thresholds where justified.
Observation Slides.management_response_action_plan: Finance Operations to configure expense module to require receipt upload and implement automated flags for missing documentation. Target date: 2026-03-31. Remediation owner: Finance Operations Manager, Mark Chen. Training session for employees and approvers scheduled by 2026-04-15.

Report Title Slide.report_title: General Corporate Operations - Vendor Management and IT Access Controls

Objective, Background and Scope.purpose_objective: Evaluate controls around vendor onboarding/management and IT user access provisioning to ensure vendor risk, payment integrity and logical access controls mitigate operational and information security risks.
Objective, Background and Scope.background: Third-party vendors and IT user access are critical to operations. Weak vendor due diligence or excessive IT privileges can create fraud, data leakage and continuity risks. Previous internal reviews highlighted gaps in vendor validation and access recertification.
Objective, Background and Scope.scope: Review covered vendor onboarding and master data management processes for vendors added between 2024-01-01 and 2025-12-31 (sample 25 new vendors) and IT access provisioning for 50 user accounts across finance and operations. Included review of vendor master changes, contract documentation and access entitlement lists.

Overall Internal Audit Rating.overall_conclusion_description: Significant deficiencies found in vendor due diligence and IT access controls, leaving the organization exposed to financial, operational and data security risks. Immediate remediation is required to tighten onboarding, approval workflows and access recertification processes.

Observation Slides.observation_title: Insufficient vendor due diligence and missing contract documentation
Observation Slides.details: In a sample of 25 newly onboarded vendors, 11 (44%) had incomplete due diligence: 7 lacked third-party validation (no W-9/Tax ID or equivalent), and 4 had no signed contract on file despite invoices being paid. Total paid to these 11 vendors during the review period was $1,250,000.
Observation Slides.risk_impact: Increased exposure to duplicate/fictitious vendors, tax withholding errors and contract non-compliance leading to potential financial loss and legal exposure. Absence of contracts for $420,000 in spend creates recovery and SLA enforcement risk.
Observation Slides.recommendations: Enforce mandatory vendor documentation before activation: tax forms, AML screening and signed contracts. Implement hold-back policy preventing payments for vendors without validated documentation. Centralize vendor master with workflow approval and periodic duplicate vendor detection.
Observation Slides.management_response_action_plan: Procurement will enforce 'no pay' activation rule and implement mandatory vendor checklist in the vendor onboarding system. Target date: 2026-05-31. Remediation owner: Procurement Director, Omar Patel. Procurement and AP to reconcile vendor master and complete missing documentation for the 11 vendors by 2026-04-30.

Observation Slides.observation_title: Excessive IT access privileges and lack of periodic access recertification
Observation Slides.details: From a review of 50 user accounts, 18 accounts (36%) held privileges inconsistent with role-based least privilege principles (e.g., finance clerks with payroll admin rights). No evidence of formal access recertification for these users in the last 12 months. One user account showed remote VPN access despite separation requirements.
Observation Slides.risk_impact: Excessive privileges increase risk of data manipulation, unauthorized transactions and data exfiltration. Lack of recertification increases residual access risk; potential impact includes unauthorized changes to payroll or vendor records.
Observation Slides.recommendations: Implement role-based access control (RBAC) model and enforce least-privilege assignments. Conduct mandatory access recertification semi-annually for critical systems. Disable dormant accounts and enforce MFA for remote access.
Observation Slides.management_response_action_plan: CISO to implement RBAC pilot for Finance and Operations and schedule first recertification sweep. Target date for RBAC pilot: 2026-06-30. Remediation owner: CISO, Laura Martins. MFA rollout for remote access to be completed by 2026-05-15; recertification process to be executed starting 2026-06-01.
